<reflection>
The first experiment provided baseline data, but the negative log-likelihood values for most mechanisms are very close, with M6 and M3 slightly better than others. M4 and M5 are clearly worse and can be considered ruled out. The small differences indicate that the moderate condition (S=2.0, cat=0.01, P=0.0) is not sufficiently discriminatory among the remaining 18 mechanisms. The aim of the first experiment was to obtain initial data; it succeeded in eliminating two mechanisms but left high uncertainty.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To discriminate among the many plausible mechanisms, I propose increasing the catalyst concentration to 0.05 M while keeping substrate at 2.0 M and no initial product. This change will amplify nonlinear effects dependent on catalyst concentration. Mechanisms involving dimerization (e.g., M2, M3, M19) predict a greater-than-linear increase in rate with catalyst, while simple mechanisms (e.g., M1) predict a linear scaling. Bimolecular deactivation steps (e.g., M13, M18, M19) will become more pronounced at higher catalyst, potentially causing faster decay of activity. In contrast, unimolecular deactivation mechanisms (e.g., M9, M14) will show less dependence on catalyst concentration. This experiment should spread out the predictions across multiple mechanistic classes, providing clearer distinctions in the fitted likelihoods.
</hypothesis>
